dish: Greek omelet — an American-cheese omelet smothered in Erie Greek sauce, served with the same slow-cooked meat sauce over hot dogs and fries
w: A 1948 Silk City diner in Lawrence Park and the only 'dinor' — the northwest-PA spelling — on the National Register of Historic Places (2004). Seventy-five-plus years of counter-service classics, most famously the Greek omelet drowned in Erie's signature Greek sauce.

dish: Fried Lake Erie perch and blackened walleye, plus langostino-crab cakes, on Dobbins Landing
w: A nautical-themed bayfront seafood house on Dobbins Landing beneath the Bicentennial Tower, its grapevine-shaded patio a summer institution. The kitchen leans on the Great Lakes catch — fresh perch and walleye — that defines Erie fish dining.

dish: Elevated New American plates — teriyaki salmon, steaks and pasta — with retractable-glass Bayfront sunset dining
w: On the 8th floor of the Bayfront Hampton Inn with floor-to-ceiling glass over Presque Isle Bay and the U.S. Brig Niagara, named for Oliver Hazard Perry. A repeat Erie Reader 'Best of Erie' winner (Best Waterfront Dining, Best Romantic Restaurant) and Only In Your State's most-romantic-in-PA pick.

dish: Knish hash and cinnamon 'flips' — creative scratch breakfast and brunch
w: A tiny downtown-Edinboro breakfast-and-brunch spot ranked #1 in town, dealing in inventive hashes (knish hash, pulled-pork hash) and its signature cinnamon 'flips.' Voted Erie Reader's Best Brunch (2025).

dish: Small-batch honey mead by flight, glass or bottle — peach-lemon, blackberry-lime — with tacos and quesadillas
w: Crawford County's only honey-wine producer, which moved from Conneaut Lake to a family-friendly downtown-Meadville tasting room in 2022. Small-batch infused meads and cocktails paired with a short Mexican-leaning food menu.

dish: Award-winning estate wines from Pennsylvania's oldest operating winery, on Twelve Mile Creek
w: Founded 1964 by Doug Moorhead and one of the first two PA wineries to open after Prohibition (1969, with Penn Shore) — the birthplace of the modern Pennsylvania wine industry, thanks to Moorhead's push for the 1968 Limited Winery Act. Both a working winery and a full home-winemaking supply store beside Twelve Mile Creek.
